To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

a cryptic fragment from the III1 module, which is exposed in the matrix form of fibronactin, localizes to lipid raft domains and stimulates cell growth, migration, contractility, and integrin signaling.
a cryptic fragment from FN's III1 module stimulates cell growth and contraction, localizes to lipid microdomains, and is required for the FN-dependent stimulation of these processes.
a fragment from the III1 module (III1H, 2–4), which is cryptic in soluble FN, localizes to lipid raft domains and differentially regulates cell growth and contractile function.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the role of matrix FN in cell growth and cytoskeletal reorganization, and suggests that the exposure of a cryptic heparin-binding site in III1 may be important for these responses.
the mechanisms by which cells respond to the extracellular matrix form of fibronctin (FN).
the mechanisms that regulate the interactions of cells with their extracellular matrix (see also the commentary in this issue by Ruoslahti, A. 1999. J. Cell Biol. 145 : 1305–1311).
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the cryptic III1H domain is an important matricryptic epitope that regulates the growth and contraction of fibroblasts through a mechanism that involves the formation of lipid rafts.
the III1 module is a matricryptin that regulates cytoskeletal dynamics and growth in part by partitioning into membrane microdomains.
a cryptic fragment from FN's III1 module is a novel ligand that interacts with a cell surface protein that is localized to caveolae and is capable of stimulating cell growth and contraction.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
matrix FN stimulates growth and contractility through the activation of a novel cryptic site within the conformational labile III1 domain of FN that localizes to lipid raft microdomains.
the III1H module of fibronectins, when presented as an intact module or as a cryptic fragment, is able to localize to lipid rafts.
the cryptic, conformationally labilized heparin-binding domain of the III1 module is a matricryptite site that is exposed on the surface of matrix fibronectin.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the conformationally sensitive III1 module is a key regulator of cell growth and contractile activity.

matrix FN is differentially regulated by integrin ligation, heparin binding, and lipid raft association, and these properties are required to stimulate changes in cell growth and cytoskeletal reorganization.

matrix FN can be partitioned into lipid rafts by virtue of its interaction with heparan sulfate, and the exposure of cryptic sites within FN can initiate signaling cascades that modulate cytoskeletal organization.
